project.title: Little Red Riding Hood: The Woodland Path
project.description: A full-featured animated fairy-tale episode demonstrating World Graph Studio story development, production planning, sound design, asset intent, storyboards, sequencing, and editorial metadata.

world.name: Woodland Village and the Old Forest
world.description: A close-knit rural village borders an ancient forest whose winding path leads to Grandmother's cottage. Familiar daylight spaces become uncertain as the trees close in, but communal care remains stronger than the dangers in the wood.
world.timeline: The episode unfolds over one autumn day: Red leaves the village in the morning, meets the Wolf near midday, reaches Grandmother's cottage at dusk, and returns safely by early evening.
world.rules: Animals may speak, but most conceal that gift from villagers. Paths remember travelers and seem to lengthen when someone acts with deceptive intent. A promise freely made carries social and symbolic weight.
world.themes: Discernment, keeping promises without surrendering curiosity, intergenerational trust, and the protection created by a caring community.
world.geography: The village sits east of the Old Forest. A marked path runs west past a creek and pine ridge to Grandmother's cottage. Woodland Warden markers identify safe crossings and emergency meeting points.
world.references: European oral fairy-tale traditions, hand-painted storybooks, practical miniature forests, warm candlelit interiors, and restrained theatrical staging.

characters.name: Little Red Riding Hood
characters.description: A thoughtful young courier learning how to balance independence with the wisdom offered by her community.
characters.appearance: A small, alert girl in a weathered scarlet wool cloak, sturdy walking boots, and a cream linen dress. She carries a woven basket with a red checked lining.
characters.personality: Curious, compassionate, observant, and determined; polite enough to listen, but brave enough to question a story that does not fit the evidence.
characters.motivation: Deliver food and medicine to Grandmother, keep her promise to stay on the marked path, and prove she can be trusted with a journey of her own.
characters.backstory: Red has grown up hearing the Woodland Wardens' safety stories. This is her first trip to Grandmother's cottage without an adult companion.
characters.voice_profile: Clear young alto with quick, precise phrasing; warmth replaces caution when she feels safe, while fear makes her speak more deliberately rather than more loudly.

characters.name: Grandmother
characters.description: An experienced herbalist whose calm attention helps Red understand that wisdom can be practiced rather than merely inherited.
characters.appearance: Silver hair braided around her head, kind dark eyes, a plum house dress, knitted shawl, and flour-dusted apron.
characters.personality: Patient, dryly funny, resourceful, and protective without being controlling.
characters.motivation: Keep Red safe, preserve her independence at the woodland cottage, and teach through questions instead of fear.
characters.backstory: Grandmother helped establish the Woodland Wardens' marked path and knows old remedies, animal tracks, and every change in the forest light.
characters.voice_profile: Low, textured contralto with measured pauses and an intimate storytelling cadence.

characters.name: Wolf
characters.description: A clever forest predator who relies on charm, speed, and other people's assumptions more than brute force.
characters.appearance: A rangy charcoal-gray wolf with amber eyes, a torn left ear, unusually expressive brows, and silent paws stained with pine resin.
characters.personality: Patient, theatrical, vain, opportunistic, and easily unsettled when someone notices a flaw in his performance.
characters.motivation: Reach Grandmother's cottage first, take control of the house, and lure Red close enough to seize the basket and its provisions.
characters.backstory: The Wolf learned scraps of human speech by watching travelers near the marked path and has used borrowed manners to hide predatory intent.
characters.voice_profile: Velvety baritone with careful consonants; the cultivated warmth frays into a rough growl when his deception fails.

characters.name: The Woodsman
characters.description: Leader of the Woodland Wardens and a dependable neighbor who treats preparedness as a shared civic practice rather than heroic spectacle.
characters.appearance: Broad-shouldered, with a moss-green coat, leather gloves, a trimmed dark beard, and a brass storm lantern marked with the Warden emblem.
characters.personality: Steady, practical, attentive, humble, and reassuring under pressure.
characters.motivation: Maintain the safe path, answer Red's emergency call, and protect the village without teaching children that courage belongs only to adults.
characters.backstory: A former carpenter, he organized the Wardens after a winter storm isolated several woodland homes. Grandmother taught him the oldest forest routes.
characters.voice_profile: Grounded mid-range voice with unhurried delivery, soft rural vowels, and a firm command tone used sparingly.

locations.name: Red's Village Cottage
locations.description: A whitewashed cottage beside the village square, with a herb garden, blue shutters, and a bench where the Woodland Wardens check their route markers.
locations.geography: Eastern edge of Woodland Village, where the cobbled lane becomes the marked forest path.
locations.mood: Safe, bustling, and warmly domestic, with a faint sense of departure at the tree line.

locations.name: Old Forest Path
locations.description: A narrow path beneath ancient pine and beech trees, crossed by roots and shafts of cold green light. Small brass Warden markers gleam at each fork.
locations.geography: Runs west from the village, over a shallow creek and along a pine ridge toward Grandmother's cottage.
locations.mood: Beautiful but watchful; birdsong and open light gradually give way to stillness and deep shadow.

locations.name: Grandmother's Woodland Cottage
locations.description: A small timber cottage with a steep roof, a kitchen full of drying herbs, and a bedroom lit by one leaded-glass window and a brass bedside candle.
locations.geography: A clearing west of the pine ridge, beside an old well and the final Woodland Warden marker.
locations.mood: Normally intimate and restorative; during the Wolf's deception, familiar details feel subtly displaced and claustrophobic.

props.name: Red Wool Cloak
props.description: A weathered scarlet wool cloak with a deep hood, wooden toggle, and a small stitched repair at the right shoulder.
props.purpose: Red's visual identifier and a continuity marker that remains readable through changing forest light.
props.notes: Keep the right-shoulder repair visible in close shots; the hood is down in the village, raised in the forest, and lowered after the rescue.

props.name: Provision Basket
props.description: A sturdy willow basket lined with red checked cloth and packed with bread, preserves, tea, and wrapped medicine.
props.purpose: The delivery objective, a source of visual business, and the item whose safety represents Red's promise.
props.notes: The medicine remains beneath the bread. The handle is in Red's right hand on the path and the lining stays tied until Scene 4.

props.name: Grandmother's Carved Bed
props.description: An old oak bed with a tall carved headboard, patchwork quilt, linen curtains, and enough depth for the Wolf to hide his silhouette.
props.purpose: Provides the familiar frame that makes the Wolf's imperfect disguise legible to Red and the audience.
props.notes: The blue quilt corner is folded back before the Wolf arrives and reversed after he climbs into bed; preserve that continuity clue.

props.name: Woodland Warden Lantern
props.description: A brass storm lantern with green glass side panels and the pine-tree emblem of the Woodland Wardens.
props.purpose: Marks the safe path in Scene 1 and announces the Woodsman's arrival through moving green light in Scene 4.
props.notes: The left panel carries a hairline crack. Its green light should precede the Woodsman into frame during the rescue.

organizations.name: Woodland Wardens
organizations.description: A volunteer village organization that maintains trail markers, checks isolated cottages, and teaches travelers how to signal for help without treating the forest as an enemy.
organizations.goals: Keep the marked path passable, connect remote neighbors to the village, document changes in animal behavior, and make practical safety knowledge available to every child.

episodes.title: The Woodland Path
episodes.synopsis: On her first solo delivery to Grandmother, Red follows the marked woodland path, recognizes the Wolf's deception, and uses a Warden signal to bring help without surrendering her own agency.

scenes.title: The Assignment
scenes.summary: Red accepts the delivery while the Woodsman checks the final Warden marker and reminds her how to call for help.
scenes.script_content:
EXT. RED'S VILLAGE COTTAGE - MORNING

Autumn light warms the cottage garden. RED secures the checked lining over her basket while THE WOODSMAN tests a brass lantern beside the first trail marker.

WOODSMAN
The forest is calm this morning, but calm is not the same as empty.

RED
I will stay on the marked path and keep the basket closed.

The Woodsman turns the lantern so its green panels flash against the trees.

WOODSMAN
If danger finds you, lift the hood, call twice, and look for this green light.

Red raises her hood, takes the basket, and steps from cobbles onto the woodland path.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: The forest is calm this morning, but calm is not the same as empty.
dialogue.description: He checks the lantern wick without trying to frighten her.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: I will stay on the marked path and keep the basket closed.
dialogue.description: Red tightens the basket lining.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: If danger finds you, lift the hood, call twice, and look for this green light.
dialogue.description: He turns the lantern so the Warden color catches the trees.

scenes.emotional_tone: Warm responsibility with a quiet edge of anticipation
scenes.production_notes: Begin with open village ambience and warm backlight. Establish the lantern's green panels and cloak repair clearly because both become continuity signals later.

scenes.title: The Encounter
scenes.summary: The Wolf tests Red's promise with flattery and a false shortcut, but she notices that he avoids every Warden marker.
scenes.script_content:
EXT. OLD FOREST PATH - MIDDAY

The marked path narrows beneath dark pines. RED walks with the basket tucked against her hip. A WOLF steps from behind a beech tree as if joining a conversation already in progress.

WOLF
Hello, little traveler. Where does such an important basket need to be?

RED
Grandmother's cottage, by the old well. I am keeping to the marked path.

The Wolf smiles and circles past a brass marker without touching its pool of light.

WOLF
Then you should take my shortcut. It is quicker, and the flowers are finer.

RED
A path that avoids every marker is not a shortcut meant for me.

A branch cracks uphill. While Red looks toward it, the Wolf vanishes between the trees.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: Hello, little traveler. Where does such an important basket need to be?
dialogue.description: He presents curiosity as courtesy.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Grandmother's cottage, by the old well. I am keeping to the marked path.
dialogue.description: Red keeps walking rather than accepting his pace.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: Then you should take my shortcut. It is quicker, and the flowers are more beautiful.
dialogue.description: He gestures toward an unmarked trail.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: A path that avoids every marker is not a shortcut meant for me.
dialogue.description: She notices pine resin on his paws and grips the basket handle.

scenes.emotional_tone: Polite tension sharpening into alert suspicion
scenes.production_notes: Cool the palette as the exchange progresses. Keep a Warden marker in the deep background of Red's coverage and exclude it from the Wolf's singles.

scenes.title: The Reveal
scenes.summary: At the cottage, Red reads the displaced details in Grandmother's room, exposes the Wolf's disguise, and calls the Warden signal before he can close the distance.
scenes.script_content:
INT. GRANDMOTHER'S WOODLAND COTTAGE - DUSK

The cottage is too still. RED sets the basket by the bed. Beneath the reversed blue quilt, the WOLF wears Grandmother's cap and keeps his torn ear pressed flat. A muffled knock sounds from the pantry.

RED
Something seems different.

WOLF
Come closer, my dear. The room is only dim.

RED
Grandmother, what big eyes you have.

WOLF
The better to see what you have brought me.

RED
And what big ears you have.

WOLF
The better to hear every little promise.

Red notices the quilt corner, the pine resin, and the hidden torn ear. She raises her hood.

RED
Oh, Grandmother. What big teeth you have.

WOLF
The better to eat you with!

The Wolf throws off the cap. Red backs to the window and calls into the clearing.

RED
You are not Grandmother! Warden! Warden!

Green light flickers between the trees outside.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Something seems different here, Grandmother.
dialogue.description: She studies the reversed quilt corner.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: Come closer, my dear. The room is very dim.
dialogue.description: He imitates Grandmother's cadence but rushes the final word.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Grandmother, what big eyes you have.
dialogue.description: Red remains beside the basket.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: The better to see what you have brought me.
dialogue.description: His gaze drops to the provisions.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: And what big ears you have.
dialogue.description: She sees the torn ear slip free of the cap.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: The better to hear every little promise.
dialogue.description: His polished voice roughens.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Oh, Grandmother. What big teeth you have.
dialogue.description: Red raises her hood and shifts toward the window.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: The better to eat you with!
dialogue.description: He throws off the disguise and lunges from the bed.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: You are not Grandmother! Warden! Warden!
dialogue.description: She calls through the open window without dropping the basket between them.

scenes.emotional_tone: Claustrophobic investigation breaking into decisive alarm
scenes.production_notes: Reverse the quilt corner established in the Asset and Storyboard. Let the room tone disappear before the torn ear is revealed. The first green lantern reflection lands after Red's second call.

scenes.title: The Rescue and Return
scenes.summary: The Woodsman's green lantern interrupts the Wolf's attack, Red frees Grandmother, and the reunited neighbors send the Wolf back into the unmarked forest.
scenes.script_content:
EXT./INT. GRANDMOTHER'S WOODLAND COTTAGE - EARLY EVENING

Green lantern light sweeps across the bedroom wall. THE WOODSMAN fills the doorway, calm and empty-handed, while the WOLF freezes between RED and the bed.

WOODSMAN
Step away from the child and face the open door.

WOLF
This is no concern of yours, Warden.

RED
Grandmother is in the pantry. I heard her answer.

Red keeps the bed between herself and the Wolf as the Woodsman opens a clear path outside. The Wolf bolts through it and disappears beyond the final marker. Red frees GRANDMOTHER, who takes her hands.

GRANDMOTHER
You noticed what fear hoped you would overlook.

RED
I kept the promise, but I also changed the plan.

WOODSMAN
That is what a good path is for. It brings help close enough to choose.

Grandmother unties the basket lining. They share bread and tea as the lantern glows on the windowsill.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: Step away from the child and face the open door.
dialogue.description: He holds the lantern high and leaves the escape route visible.

dialogue.speaker: Wolf
dialogue.line: This is no concern of yours, Warden.
dialogue.description: The cultivated voice has collapsed into a growl.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: Grandmother is in the pantry. I heard her answer.
dialogue.description: Red keeps the bed between herself and the Wolf.

dialogue.speaker: Grandmother
dialogue.line: You noticed what fear hoped you would overlook.
dialogue.description: She takes Red's hands after being freed.

dialogue.speaker: Little Red Riding Hood
dialogue.line: I kept the promise, but I also changed the plan.
dialogue.description: Relief arrives as a small, proud smile.

dialogue.speaker: The Woodsman
dialogue.line: That is what a good path is for. It brings help close enough to choose.
dialogue.description: He sets the green lantern on the windowsill.

scenes.emotional_tone: Controlled intervention resolving into relief, warmth, and earned confidence
scenes.production_notes: The Woodsman does not strike the Wolf; staging prioritizes a safe exit and Red's agency. Restore warm ambience gradually after Grandmother enters frame. End on the basket, lantern, and repaired family tableau.

shots.title: Village Cottage Establishing
shots.description: Morning village activity frames Red's cottage, the path entrance, and the Woodsman checking a brass marker.
shots.editorial_notes: Open from black on birds and cart wheels; hold long enough to read the safe geography.

shots.title: Basket and Promise
shots.description: Red secures the basket while answering the Woodsman's warning in a balanced two-shot.
shots.editorial_notes: Cut on Red tightening the checked lining; preserve both hands for prop continuity.

shots.title: Green Lantern Signal
shots.description: The Woodsman turns the lantern; green light crosses Red's raised hood and the first path marker.
shots.editorial_notes: Use as the visual match for the lantern reflection in Scene 3.

shots.title: Forest Path Establishing
shots.description: Red appears small beneath the pines while the marked path remains a bright line through the composition.
shots.editorial_notes: Transition from warm village gold to cool forest green over the first two seconds.

shots.title: Wolf Enters the Path
shots.description: The Wolf steps from behind a beech tree and settles into Red's walking pace without crossing a brass marker's light.
shots.editorial_notes: Let leaf movement announce him one beat before his muzzle enters frame.

shots.title: Red Rejects the Shortcut
shots.description: Over the Wolf's shoulder, Red notices resin on his paw and aligns herself with the next Warden marker.
shots.editorial_notes: Rack focus from the stained paw to the marker before Red delivers her final line.

shots.title: Grandmother's Room
shots.description: Red enters the dim bedroom; the bed, reversed quilt corner, basket landing place, pantry door, and window share one readable frame.
shots.editorial_notes: Hold the geography before dialogue so later evasive movement remains clear.

shots.title: Details Do Not Match
shots.description: Red's gaze connects the quilt, pine resin, and torn ear while the room falls unnaturally silent.
shots.editorial_notes: Build three inserts into one reaction rhythm, then return to Red before the teeth question.

shots.title: Wolf Revealed
shots.description: The cap falls, the Wolf bares his teeth, and Red's raised hood remains sharp at the frame edge as she calls for help.
shots.editorial_notes: End on the first green reflection rather than the lunge itself.

shots.title: Lantern at the Door
shots.description: Moving green light reaches the bedroom before the Woodsman fills the doorway and establishes an open route outside.
shots.editorial_notes: Match the lantern flare from Shot 3 and avoid framing the Woodsman as an attacking silhouette.

shots.title: The Safe Exit
shots.description: Red uses the bed as cover while the Woodsman opens a clear path and the Wolf chooses flight.
shots.editorial_notes: Play the intervention in one readable master; cut only when the Wolf crosses the threshold.

shots.title: Lantern, Basket, and Home
shots.description: Grandmother, Red, and the Woodsman share bread beside the open basket while the green lantern warms the window.
shots.editorial_notes: Finish on Red lowering her hood; dissolve to the marked path at evening.

sounds.title: Opening Narration
sounds.description: A warm storybook introduction over the village establishing shot.
sounds.spoken_text: At the edge of the Old Forest, every safe journey began with a promise and a path.
sounds.production_notes: Intimate and reassuring, with enough restraint to leave room for the coming uncertainty.

sounds.title: Red Remembers the Promise
sounds.description: Red silently rehearses the practical parts of the Woodsman's warning as the forest closes in.
sounds.spoken_text: Markers ahead, basket closed, two calls if I need the green light.
sounds.production_notes: Close, dry recording with no theatrical echo; confident rather than anxious.

sounds.title: Stay to the Marked Path
sounds.description: A cautious traveling theme whose steady pulse becomes uncertain when the Wolf appears.
sounds.lyrics:
Stay to the markers through shadow and pine.
Carry your promise and follow the sign.
sounds.production_notes: Sparse strings, celesta, and a soft frame drum; leave a midrange pocket for dialogue.

sounds.title: Old Forest Ambience
sounds.description: Layered wind, distant birds, creek water, and occasional branch movement that thins during the Wolf's approach.
sounds.production_notes: Maintain a recognizable high bird call until Shot 5, then remove it without an obvious fade.

sounds.title: Wolf Approaches Through Leaves
sounds.description: Measured paw falls and leaf crunches synchronized to the Wolf joining Red's pace.
sounds.production_notes: Use damp leaves and soft leather rather than exaggerated claws; the final step lands outside marker light.

sounds.title: Wolf Reveal Sting
sounds.description: A short designed impact as the cap falls and the Wolf's real silhouette replaces the disguise.
sounds.production_notes: Combine bowed metal and low drum; avoid a horror-style jump-scare peak.

sounds.title: Silence Before the Reveal
sounds.description: A deliberate removal of room tone while Red assembles the visual clues.
sounds.production_notes: Retain only Red's breath and one quilt movement so the silence feels subjective rather than like a technical dropout.

sounds.title: Warden Lantern and Door
sounds.description: Lantern handle, firm boots, and the cottage door opening as the Woodsman arrives.
sounds.production_notes: Lead with the small brass handle rattle so the established lantern motif arrives before the heavier door sound.

sounds.title: Closing Narration
sounds.description: A brief closing thought over the shared meal and evening path.
sounds.spoken_text: A promise was not a fence around Red's courage. It was a path that let courage find its way home.
sounds.production_notes: Use the opening narrator with slightly brighter presence and let the last word overlap the dissolve.
